bottleneck.description: World's largest zircon producer (~20% global share) and developer of Australia's first integrated rare earths refinery at Eneabba (2027 start) under a A$1.65B Australian Government Critical Minerals Facility loan.

dependency.key_customers: Pigment producers (Chemours, Kronos, Tronox), ceramic tile makers, foundry; future REE customers TBD
dependency.key_suppliers: Internal mineral sands stockpiles; Northern Minerals third-party REE feed; Fluor EPCM

editorial.notes: Iluka has dual bottleneck dimensions: zircon/mineral sands (Jacinth-Ambrosia, Balranald) where it is the largest single producer but with global substitutes (Rio/Tronox/Kenmare/Base Resources); plus a near-term, government-funded integrated REE refinery at Eneabba that will be one of the few non-Chinese light+heavy REE separation facilities. Today, neither line individually qualifies as HIGH (zircon is competitive; REE refinery is pre-commissioning, slipped to 2027 with capex now A$1.7-1.8B). MEDIUM is appropriate — strategic Western critical-minerals infrastructure but with viable substitution and execution risk.
